spotlight.title: 100 Facts About Bread
spotlight.subtitle: The Food That Built Civilization
spotlight.description: It is 14,000 years old. It has been the foundation of every major human civilization. When it runs out, revolutions begin. 100 foundational facts about the food that fed the world.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Empire State Building
books.subtitle: A Plane Once Crashed Into It
books.description: In 1945 a B-25 bomber flew into the 79th floor on a foggy morning. The building survived. So did some of the people inside. 100 electrifying facts about New York's most legendary skyscraper.

books.title: 100 Facts About Blackbeard
books.subtitle: The Most Feared Pirate Who Ever Sailed the Caribbean
books.description: Blackbeard tied lit cannon fuses into his beard before battle so his face appeared to smoke like a demon — and his reputation alone was enough to make ships surrender without firing a shot. He was killed in 1718 and it took five sword wounds and five bullets to stop him. 100 facts about the pirate who turned his own appearance into the most terrifying weapon he had.

books.title: 100 Facts About Julius Caesar
books.subtitle: The Roman General Who Made Himself Dictator for Life
books.description: Caesar was kidnapped by pirates as a young man, charmed his captors for 38 days, then returned with a fleet and had them crucified. He rewrote the Roman calendar, conquered Gaul in eight years, and was stabbed 23 times by his closest allies. 100 facts about the man who turned the Roman Republic into an empire and paid for it with his life.

books.title: 100 Facts About Nebulae
books.subtitle: The Universe's Greatest Art
books.description: The universe's greatest art — vast clouds of gas and dust where stars are born and die. 100 colorful and cosmic facts about the universe's most beautiful objects.

books.title: 100 Facts About Anubis
books.subtitle: The Egyptian God Who Judged the Dead
books.description: Anubis weighed every human heart against a feather — if your heart was heavier, a monster ate it and you ceased to exist forever. He was also the god who invented embalming. 100 facts about the jackal-headed god who decided who got to live forever.

books.title: 100 Facts About The King Cobra
books.subtitle: One Bite Kills an Elephant
books.description: It is the longest venomous snake in the world and delivers enough neurotoxin in a single bite to kill an elephant. It also builds nests and guards its eggs. 100 commanding facts about the snake that rules them all.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Golden Retriever
books.subtitle: The Dog That Became America's Favorite Family Companion
books.description: Golden Retrievers were bred in the Scottish Highlands in the 1860s to retrieve shot waterfowl without damaging them — their mouths are so gentle they can carry a raw egg without cracking it. 100 facts about the dog whose temperament is so consistent it seems almost engineered for human love.

books.title: 100 Facts About Star-Nosed Moles
books.subtitle: The Star-Faced Digger
books.description: With 22 pink tentacles on its face and the fastest eating speed of any mammal, this creature is pure biological madness. 100 wild facts.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Milky Way
books.subtitle: The Galaxy We Call Home
books.description: We live inside it but can never see it whole. A spiral galaxy of 400 billion stars — and we're on one tiny arm. 100 breathtaking facts about the galaxy we call home.

books.title: 100 Facts About Cheese
books.subtitle: The Most Stolen Food on the Planet
books.description: It is the most shoplifted food item in the world. It has over 1,800 documented varieties. Some of it is legally required to be made within a specific radius of a specific village. 100 aged facts about the world's most obsessively crafted food.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Maine Coon
books.subtitle: The Gentle Giant That Won America's First Cat Show
books.description: A Maine Coon named Cosey won the very first major American cat show at Madison Square Garden in 1895 — and the breed has never stopped competing since. They can weigh up to 18 pounds, chirp instead of meow, and love water. 100 facts about America's original giant cat.

books.title: 100 Facts About The German Shepherd
books.subtitle: The World's Most Versatile Working Dog
books.description: German Shepherds serve as police dogs, military dogs, guide dogs, search and rescue dogs, and bomb detection dogs — often switching roles within a single career. The breed was created in 1899 by one man with a very specific vision. 100 facts about the dog that can do almost any job better than any other breed.

books.title: 100 Facts About Big Ben
books.subtitle: It's Not Even Big Ben
books.description: The name everyone uses refers to the bell inside the tower, not the tower itself. And that is just the beginning of what most people get wrong. 100 surprising facts about London's most misunderstood landmark.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Spartan Warrior
books.subtitle: The Most Brutally Trained Soldier Who Ever Lived
books.description: Spartan boys were taken from their mothers at age seven and not allowed to return home until they were thirty. They trained by being deliberately starved. 100 facts about the military machine that turned cruelty into a philosophy.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Ragdoll
books.subtitle: The Cat That Goes Limp in Your Arms Like a Rag Doll
books.description: The Ragdoll breed was created by a single woman in California in the 1960s who claimed her cat had been altered by a car accident — a myth that persisted for decades. What is real is that they go completely limp when held and follow their owners around like dogs. 100 facts about the most docile and affectionate large cat breed in existence.

books.title: 100 Facts About Wine
books.subtitle: Ten Thousand Years in a Glass
books.description: The oldest evidence of winemaking dates back 8,000 years. It has been central to religion, medicine, trade, and every major civilization since. 100 intoxicating facts about the world's most storied drink.

books.title: 100 Facts About Medusa
books.subtitle: The Gorgon Whose Gaze Turned Men to Stone
books.description: Medusa was not born a monster — she was transformed into one by Athena as punishment for being assaulted in her own temple. The original myth is a story of divine injustice. 100 facts about the most misunderstood figure in Greek mythology.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Black Mamba
books.subtitle: The Snake That Doesn't Miss
books.description: It is the fastest snake on Earth, can strike up to 12 times in a single attack, and without antivenom its bite is nearly always fatal. 100 gripping facts about Africa's most feared serpent.

books.title: 100 Facts About Odin
books.subtitle: The All-Father Who Sacrificed His Eye for Wisdom
books.description: Odin hung himself from the World Tree for nine days with a spear through his side to discover the secrets of the runes. He also traded his eye to drink from the well of cosmic knowledge. 100 facts about the Norse god who was obsessed with his own death.

books.title: 100 Facts About Comets

books.title: 100 Facts About The Labrador Retriever
books.subtitle: The Family Dog That Held America's Top Spot for 31 Years

books.title: 100 Facts About The Samurai

books.title: 100 Facts About Beer

books.title: 100 Facts About The Persian Cat

books.title: 100 Facts About The Box Jellyfish

books.title: 100 Facts About Sugar

books.title: 100 Facts About The Indus Valley Civilization
books.subtitle: Millions Left No Trace
books.description: A Bronze Age supercivilization of over a million people with running water, city planning, and no armies — that vanished without a war. 100 extraordinary facts about history's most peaceful lost empire.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Minoans
books.subtitle: Europe's First Civilization
books.description: Europe's first great civilization built palaces, traded across the Mediterranean, and collapsed completely around 1450 BC with no clear explanation. 100 fascinating facts about the ancient world's greatest vanishing act.

books.title: 100 Facts About Cahokia
books.subtitle: North America's Lost Metropolis
books.description: A pre-Columbian city larger than London that rose, thrived, and was completely abandoned centuries before Europeans arrived. 100 stunning facts about America's forgotten ancient metropolis.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Khmer Empire
books.subtitle: Swallowed by the Jungle
books.description: They built Angkor Wat, ruled Southeast Asia for centuries, and then disappeared into the jungle they had conquered. 100 incredible facts about the empire the trees took back.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Cochno Stone
books.subtitle: Scotland's Unreadable Stone Map
books.description: A 6,000-year-old slab covered in mysterious cup-and-ring markings — the largest collection of Bronze Age rock art in Europe — with a purpose nobody has ever explained. 100 extraordinary facts about Scotland's buried enigma.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Franklin Expedition
books.subtitle: Ice Defeated Britain
books.description: Britain's most advanced Arctic expedition sailed in 1845 with 129 men, two warships, and enough supplies for years. None of them came back. 100 frozen facts about the Royal Navy's greatest disaster.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Flannan Isles Lighthouse
books.subtitle: Keepers Who Vanished
books.description: In December 1900 three experienced lighthouse keepers vanished from a remote Scottish island. An overturned chair, a half-eaten meal, oilskins still hanging. No bodies. No explanation. 100 haunting facts about one of history's most baffling disappearances.

books.title: 100 Facts About Percy Fawcett
books.subtitle: The Jungle Kept Him Forever
books.description: A legendary British explorer walked into the Amazon in 1925 searching for a lost city of gold and was never seen again. 100 extraordinary facts about history's most famous disappearance.

books.title: 100 Facts About The USS Cyclops
books.subtitle: Vanished Without a Trace
books.description: A US Navy collier carrying 309 men vanished in 1918 without a distress signal, a wreck, or a single body ever found. 100 haunting facts about the Navy's greatest unsolved loss.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Anasazi
books.subtitle: The Cliff Builders That Moved On
books.description: They carved entire cities into canyon walls, mastered desert survival for centuries, and then abandoned everything overnight. 100 remarkable facts about the Ancient Pueblo people who left without looking back.

books.title: 100 Facts About Linear A
books.subtitle: The Script No One Can Crack
books.description: The ancient Minoan writing system has over 1,500 known inscriptions and has defeated every codebreaker for over 100 years. Every other ancient script has been deciphered. Not this one. 100 fascinating facts about history's most stubborn unsolved language.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Dorabella Cipher
books.subtitle: Elgar's Secret Message
books.description: In 1897 composer Edward Elgar sent a friend a letter written in a code nobody has ever cracked. 100 fascinating facts about music's most enduring encrypted secret.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Beale Ciphers
books.subtitle: Millions Hidden Behind Code
books.description: Three encrypted documents. One decoded. Two still unbroken. And supposedly a fortune in gold and silver buried somewhere in Virginia waiting for whoever cracks them. 100 addictive facts about the world's most valuable unsolved code.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Circleville Letters
books.subtitle: Terror From an Anonymous Pen
books.description: For nearly two decades, anonymous threatening letters terrorized residents of a small Ohio town. One person was convicted. The letters kept coming from prison. The writer was never identified. 100 gripping facts about America's most disturbing unsolved correspondence.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Taman Shud Case
books.subtitle: The Mystery Man of Somerton Beach
books.description: A dead man on an Australian beach with no identity, no cause of death, a hidden note with an uncracked code, and zero answers 75 years later. 100 gripping facts about the world's most baffling cold case.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Amber Room
books.subtitle: Looted and Never Found
books.description: Called the Eighth Wonder of the World, the Amber Room was looted by the Nazis in 1941 and has never been seen since. 100 dazzling facts about history's most valuable missing masterpiece.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Beale Treasure
books.subtitle: Millions Still Waiting Underground
books.description: Somewhere in Bedford County, Virginia, a fortune in gold, silver, and jewels has been buried since the 1820s. The map exists. The code is the problem. 100 treasure-hunting facts about America's greatest buried mystery.

books.title: 100 Facts About Yamashita's Gold
books.subtitle: Treasure Hunters Still Digging
books.description: Japanese forces supposedly buried billions in looted Asian treasure across the Philippines before their defeat. Decades of digging have found tunnels, booby traps, and more questions. 100 extraordinary facts about the war fortune nobody has claimed.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Lost Dutchman Mine
books.subtitle: Arizona's Endless Hunt
books.description: Somewhere in Arizona's Superstition Mountains hides a gold mine so rich and so cursed that it has driven searchers to madness and death for over a century. 100 gripping facts about America's most dangerous treasure hunt.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Copper Scroll Treasure
books.subtitle: Ancient Wealth Still Hidden
books.description: Unlike the other Dead Sea Scrolls, this one isn't scripture. It's a treasure map listing 64 locations of hidden gold and silver worth billions. None of it has ever been found. 100 astonishing facts about the scroll that changed everything.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Yonaguni Monument
books.subtitle: Japan's Submerged Enigma
books.description: A massive underwater stone structure off the coast of Japan with terraced platforms, right angles, and no scientific consensus on whether humans built it. 100 mind-bending facts about the pyramid beneath the waves.

books.title: 100 Facts About Pavlopetri
books.subtitle: Ancient Streets Beneath the Sea
books.description: A 5,000 year old city sits perfectly preserved on the ocean floor off the coast of Greece, with streets, buildings, and courtyards still intact. 100 incredible facts about the oldest submerged city ever discovered.

books.title: 100 Facts About Dwarka
books.subtitle: India's Sunken Sacred City
books.description: Hindu scriptures described Krishna's golden city of Dwarka for thousands of years. Then divers found it submerged off the coast of India. 100 extraordinary facts about the sacred city the ocean swallowed.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Rongorongo Script
books.subtitle: Easter Island's Unbreakable Code
books.description: Twenty-seven wooden tablets covered in an undeciphered script found on Easter Island. The culture that created it was wiped out before anyone recorded its meaning. 100 remarkable facts about possibly the last independent invention of writing in human history.

books.title: 100 Facts About Heracleion
books.subtitle: Egypt's Drowned Gateway
books.description: For 1,200 years, Egypt's greatest port city lay hidden under the Mediterranean. Then divers found it almost perfectly intact. 100 stunning facts about the ancient gateway the sea reclaimed.

books.title: 100 Facts About Derinkuyu
books.subtitle: The City Under the City
books.description: Carved 18 floors straight down into Turkish rock, Derinkuyu could hide 20,000 people from any threat on the surface. 100 incredible facts about the deepest underground city ever discovered.

books.title: 100 Facts About Cappadocia
books.subtitle: City of Tunnels and Secrets
books.description: Beneath the fairy chimneys of central Turkey lies an entire underground world of tunnels, cities, and chambers carved by ancient hands. 100 fascinating facts about the civilization that moved below ground.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Sannikov Land
books.subtitle: The Island That Disappeared
books.description: Multiple credible explorers reported a large Arctic island between 1811 and 1886. Soviet expeditions were sent to find it. It was never found. 100 extraordinary facts about the island that vanished from the map.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Tunguska Event
books.subtitle: Explosion With No Crater
books.description: In 1908 an explosion 1,000 times more powerful than Hiroshima flattened 2,000 square kilometers of Siberian forest and left no crater. No fragment of whatever caused it has ever been conclusively found. 100 explosive facts about the largest impact event in recorded history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Catacombs of Paris
books.subtitle: Skulls and Bones Beneath the City of Light
books.description: Beneath the most glamorous city on earth lie 300 kilometers of tunnels holding the bones of six million people. 100 dark and gripping facts about Paris's underground empire of the dead.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Roman Dodecahedra
books.subtitle: Relics Rome Never Mentioned
books.description: Over 130 hollow bronze twelve-sided objects have been found across the Roman Empire. Not a single Roman text mentions them. Their purpose remains completely unknown. 100 baffling facts about antiquity's most mysterious artifact.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Antikythera Mechanism
books.subtitle: Ancient Tech Too Advanced
books.description: A 2,000 year old Greek device with more than 30 interlocking bronze gears that tracked the movements of the sun, moon, and planets. 100 mind-blowing facts about the world's first computer.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Lycurgus Cup
books.subtitle: The Cup That Changes Color
books.description: A 4th century Roman glass cup turns from green to red depending on where light shines through it — due to nanoparticles of gold and silver embedded in the glass. Ancient nanotechnology nobody can fully explain. 100 illuminating facts about Rome's most impossible artifact.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Phaistos Disc
books.subtitle: Minoan Message No One Can Read
books.description: A fired clay disc from 1700 BC covered in 241 stamped symbols arranged in a spiral. The only object of its kind ever found. Never deciphered. 100 remarkable facts about the most unique mystery in archaeology.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Map of the Creator
books.subtitle: The Stone That Rewrites History
books.description: A stone slab found in Russia in 1999 appears to show a detailed three-dimensional relief map of the Ural region with canals, dams, and structures that should not exist. 100 controversial facts about the discovery that divided scientists.

books.title: 100 Facts About Amelia Earhart's Disappearance
books.subtitle: The Flight That Failed the Dream
books.description: The world's most famous aviator took off to circle the globe in 1937 and was never seen again. 100 gripping facts about aviation's greatest unsolved mystery.

books.title: 100 Facts About D.B. Cooper
books.subtitle: A Ghost in the Sky
books.description: In 1971 a man hijacked a plane, extorted $200,000, parachuted into a storm over the Pacific Northwest, and was never identified or found. 100 thrilling facts about America's only unsolved air piracy case.

books.title: 100 Facts About Jimmy Hoffa's Disappearance
books.subtitle: America's Most Famous Missing Body
books.description: The most powerful union boss in American history walked into a Detroit parking lot in 1975 and was never seen again. 100 explosive facts about the disappearance that still haunts American organized crime.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Princes in the Tower
books.subtitle: Vanished for a Throne
books.description: Two young English princes were locked in the Tower of London in 1483 and never seen again. Their uncle became king. 100 royal facts about England's most chilling unsolved murder.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Sodder Children
books.subtitle: The Fire That Left No Graves
books.description: Five children vanished during a Christmas Eve house fire in 1945. No remains were ever found. Their parents never stopped believing they were alive. 100 heartbreaking facts about America's most haunting cold case.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Vatican Secret Archives
books.subtitle: History Behind Locked Doors
books.description: 85 kilometers of shelving, documents spanning 12 centuries, and access granted to almost nobody. 100 extraordinary facts about the most restricted library in human history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Beaumont Children
books.subtitle: Australia's Unsolved Beach Vanishing
books.description: On Australia Day 1966 three children aged 4, 7 and 9 walked to the beach and never came home. No bodies. No suspects charged. Australia's biggest unsolved case. 100 heartbreaking facts about the disappearance that changed a nation.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Overtoun Bridge
books.subtitle: Where Dogs Leap to Death
books.description: Since the 1950s over 600 dogs have leaped from the same spot on a Scottish stone bridge. Survivors climb back and jump again. No scientific explanation has been fully accepted. 100 haunting facts about the bridge that calls to dogs.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Oakville Blobs
books.subtitle: When It Rained Mystery
books.description: In August 1994 a gelatinous substance rained down on Oakville, Washington six times in three weeks. Residents fell ill. Lab tests found human white blood cells inside. The government tested and never fully explained it. 100 unsettling facts about the day it rained something nobody could identify.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Greenbrier Bunker
books.subtitle: Cold War Worries
books.description: For 30 years, a luxury five-star resort in West Virginia hid a fully equipped nuclear bunker designed to shelter the entire US Congress after an atomic attack. 100 classified facts about America's most elegant secret.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Death of Edgar Allan Poe
books.subtitle: Missing for Four Days
books.description: America's master of horror was found delirious on a Baltimore street in 1849, died four days later, and the cause was never established. 100 dark facts about literature's most mysterious death.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Max Headroom Broadcast Intrusion
books.subtitle: TV Hijack That Stunned America
books.description: In November 1987 an unknown person hijacked two Chicago television broadcasts wearing a Max Headroom mask, transmitted bizarre content, and was never identified despite FBI investigation. 100 electrifying facts about the most brazen unsolved broadcast intrusion in history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Black Dahlia
books.subtitle: Broken Hollywood Dream
books.description: Elizabeth Short came to Hollywood with a dream and was found murdered in a vacant lot in 1947 in the most shocking crime scene LA had ever seen. 100 haunting facts about Hollywood's most famous unsolved murder.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Death of Elisa Lam
books.subtitle: Elevator to Nowhere
books.description: A 21-year-old tourist was found dead in a rooftop water tank at the Cecil Hotel after surveillance footage of her bizarre behavior in an elevator went viral worldwide. 100 unsettling facts about the case that haunted the internet.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Death of William Desmond Taylor
books.subtitle: The Director's Last Scene
books.description: Hollywood's most powerful director was shot dead in 1922, the investigation was immediately tampered with, and no one was ever charged. 100 glamorous and gritty facts about the murder that exposed old Hollywood's darkest secrets.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Nazi Gold Train
books.subtitle: The Golden Myth
books.description: A train loaded with Nazi gold, artwork, and treasure supposedly disappeared into a Polish mountain tunnel at the end of World War Two. 100 gripping facts about Europe's most hunted buried fortune.

books.title: 100 Facts About Operation Bernhard
books.subtitle: The Audacious Pound Plot
books.description: The Nazis forged over 130 million British pounds in the most ambitious counterfeiting operation in history, using concentration camp prisoners as the workforce. 100 shocking facts about the plot that nearly broke Britain's economy.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Quedlinburg Treasures
books.subtitle: Masterpieces Stolen in War
books.description: A Texas soldier packed priceless medieval relics into his duffel bag during World War Two and hid them in a Texas cave for decades. 100 extraordinary facts about the greatest art theft in American military history.

books.title: 100 Facts About Goering's Art Hoard
books.subtitle: Looting Europe's Soul
books.description: Hermann Goering personally looted over 1,300 masterpieces from across occupied Europe, building the greatest stolen art collection in history. 100 staggering facts about the Nazi who tried to steal a civilization's culture.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Merkers Mine
books.subtitle: The Nazi Gold Vault
books.description: In April 1945 American soldiers stumbled into a German salt mine packed with Nazi gold, currency, and looted art worth billions. 100 astonishing facts about the greatest single treasure discovery of World War Two.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Hope Diamond
books.subtitle: The Curse in Blue
books.description: The world's most famous gemstone has passed through the hands of kings, collectors, and thieves, leaving a trail of misfortune, madness, and death in its wake. 100 dazzling facts about the most cursed diamond in history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Crying Boy Paintings
books.subtitle: Surviving the Inferno
books.description: Mass-produced portraits of crying children were reportedly found undamaged in the ruins of dozens of house fires across Britain in the 1980s. 100 eerie facts about the paintings the flames refused to destroy.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Dybbuk Box
books.subtitle: The Cabinet of Misfortune
books.description: A Jewish wine cabinet sold on eBay came with a warning, a history of nightmares, and a chain of owners who all reported the same terrifying experiences. 100 spine-chilling facts about the most haunted object ever listed online.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Delhi Purple Sapphire
books.subtitle: Fortune's Dark Jewel
books.description: Stolen from an Indian temple in 1857, this gemstone left a trail of illness, bankruptcy, and suicide among every owner until it was donated to a museum with a warning letter attached. 100 cursed facts about the gem nobody wanted to keep.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Basano Vase
books.subtitle: Silver Vessel of Doom
books.description: A 15th century Italian silver vase was found with a note warning of its curse. Four owners died shortly after acquiring it. A museum refused to accept it. 100 chilling facts about the vase nobody wants to own.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Ark of the Covenant
books.subtitle: Sacred Treasure Hunted Forever
books.description: The gold chest built to hold the Ten Commandments has been sought by armies, explorers, and governments for 2,500 years and has never been found. 100 extraordinary facts about history's most searched sacred object.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Holy Grail
books.subtitle: The Quest for Eternity
books.description: The cup used at the Last Supper has inspired crusades, obsessions, and centuries of searching by everyone from medieval knights to modern treasure hunters. 100 sacred facts about the most sought object in Western history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Shroud of Turin
books.subtitle: Image Science Can't Explain
books.description: A linen cloth bearing the image of a crucified man has survived fires, wars, and centuries of scientific testing without producing a definitive answer. 100 remarkable facts about the burial cloth that keeps defeating science.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Spear of Destiny
books.subtitle: Lance of Divine Power
books.description: The Roman lance that pierced Jesus at the crucifixion has been claimed by Charlemagne, Napoleon, and Hitler, each believing it granted world domination. 100 powerful facts about the weapon every conqueror wanted to own.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Lost Tablets of Gilgamesh
books.subtitle: Epic Older Than the Bible
books.description: Clay tablets over 4,000 years old tell the story of a great flood, a search for immortality, and a hero's journey that predates every holy book on earth. 100 ancient facts about humanity's oldest written epic.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Lost Roman Legion
books.subtitle: Rome's Vanished Ninth
books.description: The Ninth Legion marched into northern Britain around 120 AD and was never recorded again. No battle, no surrender, no explanation. 100 gripping facts about Rome's most famous military disappearance.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Dancing Plague of 1518
books.subtitle: When a Town Danced For Weeks
books.description: In July 1518 a woman in Strasbourg began dancing uncontrollably. Within weeks hundreds had joined her and couldn't stop. Nobody knows why. 100 bizarre facts about history's strangest mass hysteria event.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Wow! Signal
books.subtitle: Echo of Extraterrestrial Contact
books.description: On August 15, 1977 a radio telescope detected a 72-second signal so powerful and so structured that the astronomer who found it wrote WOW in the margin. It has never been detected again. 100 cosmic facts about the most compelling evidence of alien contact ever recorded.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Taos Hum
books.subtitle: Mystery Sound Heard by Few
books.description: A persistent low-frequency hum has been heard by residents of Taos, New Mexico for decades. No source has ever been identified. 100 resonating facts about the sound that drives people to madness.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Green Children of Woolpit
books.subtitle: Medieval Tale of Strangers
books.description: Two green-skinned children appeared in a 12th century English village speaking an unknown language, eating only raw beans, and claiming to come from a land without sun. 100 extraordinary facts about history's most inexplicable arrival.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Golden Gate Bridge
books.subtitle: Everyone Said It Was Impossible
books.description: Engineers said the currents were too strong, the fog too thick, the water too deep. They were wrong. 100 breathtaking facts about the bridge that defied every prediction.

books.title: 100 Facts About Buckingham Palace
books.subtitle: The Palace Full of Secrets
books.description: Behind the gates and the famous balcony lies a building with a post office, a cinema, a swimming pool, and a history far stranger than any royal biography admits. 100 fascinating facts about the world's most famous residence.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Colosseum
books.subtitle: The Greatest Show in Human History
books.description: It held 80,000 spectators. It had retractable awnings, underground tunnels, and elevators for wild animals. It hosted executions, hunts, and battles for over four centuries. 100 staggering facts about Rome's greatest arena.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Taj Mahal
books.subtitle: Built From a Broken Heart
books.description: An emperor lost his beloved wife and spent 22 years and the labor of 20,000 workers building her a tomb. Then he was imprisoned by his own son, left to stare at it from a window until he died. 100 magnificent facts about the world's greatest monument to love.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Sagrada Familia
books.subtitle: 140 Years and Still Not Finished
books.description: Construction began in 1882. The architect who took it over was killed by a tram in 1926. The building is still not complete. 100 incredible facts about the most ambitious church ever attempted.

books.title: 100 Facts About Mount Rushmore
books.subtitle: The Mountain With a Hidden Secret Chamber
books.description: Behind Lincoln's head is a sealed chamber carved into the rock, designed to hold the most important records of American civilization. Almost no one knows it exists. 100 explosive facts about the monument carved into a sacred mountain.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Leaning Tower of Pisa
books.subtitle: They Knew It Was Tilting and Kept Going
books.description: The tilt began during construction in the 12th century. They noticed. They kept building anyway. 100 astonishing facts about the engineering blunder that became one of the world's most visited monuments.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Hagia Sophia
books.subtitle: Church Then Mosque Then Museum Then Mosque Again
books.description: For nearly 1,000 years it was the largest cathedral in the world. Then it became a mosque, then a museum, then a mosque again. 100 extraordinary facts about the building that has survived empires, earthquakes, and centuries of reinvention.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Trevi Fountain
books.subtitle: One Coin, One Wish, One Million a Year
books.description: Tourists throw roughly one million euros worth of coins into this fountain every year. The money goes to charity. The wishes, as far as anyone can tell, are on their own. 100 wonderful facts about Rome's most theatrical landmark.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Acropolis of Athens
books.subtitle: Where Western Civilization Was Born
books.description: On this rocky hill above Athens, the foundations of democracy, philosophy, drama, and architecture were laid. The buildings are still standing after 2,500 years. 100 profound facts about the birthplace of the modern world.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Notre-Dame Cathedral
books.subtitle: 850 Years Standing, One Night Nearly Ended It
books.description: It survived the French Revolution, two World Wars, and centuries of neglect. Then on April 15, 2019, the world watched it burn. 100 gripping facts about Paris's most beloved cathedral.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Panama Canal
books.subtitle: 27,000 People Died to Connect Two Oceans
books.description: France tried first and failed catastrophically. The United States took over and finished what became the greatest engineering project of its era, at a devastating human cost. 100 powerful facts about the canal that changed global trade forever.

books.title: 100 Facts About Times Square
books.subtitle: The Most Photographed Spot on Earth
books.description: It was once called Longacre Square, a hub for horse trading. Today it is the most photographed location on the planet, with over 50 million visitors a year. 100 dazzling facts about New York's most electric intersection.

books.title: 100 Facts About The CN Tower
books.subtitle: 32 Years Nobody Could Touch It
books.description: From 1976 to 2009 it was the tallest free-standing structure on Earth. For 32 years nothing humans built came close. 100 towering facts about Canada's most iconic structure.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Arc de Triomphe
books.subtitle: Napoleon Never Saw It Finished
books.description: Napoleon commissioned it after his greatest victory. It took 30 years to build. He was dead before it was complete. 100 triumphant facts about Paris's most powerful monument.

books.title: 100 Facts About St. Peter's Basilica
books.subtitle: 120 Years to Build the Biggest Church on Earth
books.description: It took 120 years, 20 architects, and the labor of thousands to complete. It consumed the wealth of the Catholic Church and sparked a religious revolution. 100 monumental facts about the largest church ever built.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Kremlin
books.subtitle: Not Just a Building. A Secret City.
books.description: Behind its red walls lies a complex of palaces, cathedrals, arsenals, and secrets that has been the center of Russian power for over 500 years. 100 revealing facts about the fortress at the heart of the world's largest country.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Brandenburg Gate
books.subtitle: It Survived Two World Wars and a Wall
books.description: Napoleon marched through it. Hitler used it as a backdrop. The Berlin Wall sealed it off for 28 years. When the Wall fell, it was the first place the crowds gathered. 100 historic facts about Germany's most enduring symbol.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Great Wall of China
books.subtitle: The Biggest Thing Humans Ever Built
books.description: It stretches over 13,000 miles, took centuries to build, and required the labor of millions. It did not stop the invasions it was designed to prevent. 100 immense facts about the greatest construction project in human history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Polar Bear
books.subtitle: The Arctic's Apex Predator Has No Natural Enemies
books.description: Nothing hunts it. It can smell a seal through three feet of ice from a mile away. It is the largest land carnivore on Earth. 100 formidable facts about the white giant of the Arctic.

books.title: 100 Facts About The African Lion
books.subtitle: The King Didn't Get That Title for Nothing
books.description: It is the only cat that lives and hunts in social groups. Its roar can be heard five miles away. It sleeps 20 hours a day and wakes up ready to kill. 100 majestic facts about the apex predator of the African savanna.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Nile Crocodile
books.subtitle: It's Been Eating Everything in Its Path Since the Dinosaurs
books.description: It has barely changed in 200 million years because it has never needed to. It is responsible for hundreds of human deaths every year across Africa. 100 ferocious facts about the river's deadliest resident.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Cassowary
books.subtitle: The World's Most Dangerous Bird Looks Like a Dinosaur
books.description: It cannot fly but it can run at 30 miles per hour and deliver a kick that can disembowel a human. It is the direct descendant of theropod dinosaurs. 100 prehistoric facts about the world's most dangerous bird.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Cone Snail
books.subtitle: The Deadliest Thing in a Pretty Shell
books.description: It looks beautiful lying on the beach. Pick it up and it can fire a harpoon-like tooth that delivers venom with no known antidote. 100 lethal facts about the ocean's most deceptive killer.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Inland Taipan
books.subtitle: Drop for Drop the Most Venomous Snake Alive
books.description: A single bite contains enough venom to kill 100 adult humans. It is the most toxic venom of any land snake ever measured. 100 venomous facts about the snake that wins every comparison.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Piranha
books.subtitle: The Truth Is Scarier Than the Legend
books.description: Hollywood exaggerated the feeding frenzy. The reality of piranha biology, hunting behavior, and documented attacks is frightening enough without the fiction. 100 razor-toothed facts about the Amazon's most notorious fish.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Harpy Eagle
books.subtitle: Talons Bigger Than a Grizzly Bear's Claws
books.description: It is the most powerful eagle on Earth. Its talons are longer than the claws of a grizzly bear and strong enough to crush bone. It hunts monkeys and sloths from the jungle canopy. 100 powerful facts about the sky's apex predator.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Grizzly Bear
books.subtitle: 900 Pounds of Pure Survival Instinct
books.description: It can run faster than a horse over short distances, smell food from 18 miles away, and remember every food source it has ever visited. 100 formidable facts about North America's most powerful land predator.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Cape Buffalo
books.subtitle: The Animal That Kills the Most Hunters in Africa
books.description: It has never been domesticated. It holds grudges and has been known to ambush hunters who wounded it days earlier. It kills more big game hunters than any other animal in Africa. 100 relentless facts about the continent's most dangerous prey.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Poison Dart Frog
books.subtitle: Bright Colors Are Nature's Way of Saying Stay Away
books.description: The most toxic species carries enough poison to kill 10 adult humans. Indigenous hunters have used its secretions on blowgun darts for centuries. 100 vivid facts about the most colorful killers in the rainforest.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Brazilian Wandering Spider
books.subtitle: The World's Most Aggressive Spider Doesn't Build Webs
books.description: It does not wait in a web. It wanders. It is the most venomous spider on Earth and it actively pursues threats rather than retreating from them. 100 unsettling facts about the spider that holds the Guinness record for most toxic.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Stonefish
books.subtitle: You Won't See It Until It's Too Late
books.description: It is the most venomous fish in the world and it is virtually invisible on the ocean floor. Step on one and you will know immediately. 100 excruciating facts about the ocean's greatest camouflage artist.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Killer Whale
books.subtitle: The Ocean's Most Intelligent Apex Predator
books.description: It has no natural predators in any ocean on Earth. It teaches hunting techniques to its young, coordinates attacks with military precision, and has been documented hunting great white sharks. 100 awe-inspiring facts about the ocean's ultimate predator.

books.title: 100 Facts About The African Elephant
books.subtitle: The Largest Land Animal on Earth Doesn't Forget
books.description: It is the largest land animal alive. It mourns its dead, recognizes itself in mirrors, and has been documented returning to the bones of fallen family members years later. 100 magnificent facts about the giant that never forgets.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Tiger
books.subtitle: The Most Powerful Cat That Ever Walked the Earth
books.description: It is the largest wild cat on Earth, capable of taking down prey four times its own size. It hunts alone, strikes without warning, and leaves almost no survivors. 100 fierce facts about the planet's most powerful feline.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Wolverine
books.subtitle: Pound for Pound the Most Fearless Animal Alive
books.description: It has been documented driving grizzly bears off kills. It has no fear response that researchers can reliably trigger. Pound for pound it may be the most aggressive animal on the planet. 100 ferocious facts about the wilderness's most relentless fighter.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Deathstalker Scorpion
books.subtitle: The Most Dangerous Scorpion on the Planet
books.description: It is responsible for 75 percent of all scorpion-related deaths worldwide. Its venom is a complex cocktail of neurotoxins with no single antidote. 100 venomous facts about the desert's deadliest arachnid.

books.title: 100 Facts About Pizza
books.subtitle: How a Peasant Dish Conquered the World
books.description: It started as street food for the poor of Naples. Today it is a 145 billion dollar global industry. 100 saucy facts about the dish that went from peasant staple to planetary obsession.

books.title: 100 Facts About Hot Sauce
books.subtitle: The Science Behind the Burn
books.description: Capsaicin does not actually burn you. It tricks your brain into thinking you are on fire. Understanding why humans voluntarily seek that sensation is stranger than the sensation itself. 100 scorching facts about the world's most addictive condiment.

books.title: 100 Facts About Ice Cream
books.subtitle: The Coldest Obsession in Human History
books.description: Chinese emperors ate frozen milk mixtures 2,000 years ago. By the time it reached Europe it was a luxury only royalty could afford. Today humanity consumes 15 billion liters of it per year. 100 delicious facts about the world's most beloved frozen treat.

books.title: 100 Facts About Tea
books.subtitle: The Drink That Changed the World
books.description: It sparked a revolution in America, drove the British Empire's trade policy, and is the second most consumed beverage on Earth after water. 100 steeped facts about the drink that moved history.

books.title: 100 Facts About Sushi
books.subtitle: Not What You Think It Is
books.description: The original form of sushi had no raw fish and was not Japanese. It was a fermented preservation method invented in Southeast Asia. 100 surprising facts about the food the world thinks it understands.

books.title: 100 Facts About Mushrooms
books.subtitle: Neither Plant Nor Animal and Stranger Than Both
books.description: They are more closely related to animals than to plants. The largest living organism on Earth is a fungus. Some species can dissolve rock and communicate through underground networks. 100 extraordinary facts about the kingdom science is still figuring out.

books.title: 100 Facts About Olive Oil
books.subtitle: Liquid Gold Since Ancient Greece
books.description: The Greeks used it as currency, medicine, fuel, and cosmetic. Olympic athletes were bathed in it. Wars were fought over the trees that produced it. 100 ancient facts about the oil that built the Mediterranean world.

books.title: 100 Facts About Eggs
books.subtitle: The Most Perfect Food Ever Designed
books.description: It contains every nutrient needed to sustain life except Vitamin C. It has been eaten by every human civilization in recorded history. Its structure has never been improved upon by food science. 100 essential facts about the world's most complete food.

books.title: 100 Facts About Bananas
books.subtitle: The World's Most Complicated Fruit
books.description: The banana you eat today is a clone. The variety the world ate 60 years ago was wiped out by a fungus. The same fungus is coming for the current variety. 100 unexpected facts about the world's most popular fruit.

books.title: 100 Facts About Chili Peppers
books.subtitle: Your Brain Thinks You're on Fire
books.description: There is no heat. Capsaicin binds to pain receptors designed to detect actual burning. Your brain is being fooled every single time. 100 blazing facts about the fruit that conquered global cuisine.

books.title: 100 Facts About Butter
books.subtitle: From Sacred Offering to Breakfast Staple
books.description: Ancient cultures buried it as an offering to the gods. Medieval Europeans used it as medicine. It has been declared both deadly and essential by nutritional science in the same century. 100 rich facts about the world's most debated spread.

books.title: 100 Facts About Whiskey
books.subtitle: Water of Life and Liquid History
books.description: The word whiskey comes from the Gaelic for water of life. It has been medicine, currency, and the cause of a rebellion against the United States government. 100 aged facts about the spirit that runs through history.

books.title: 100 Facts About Pasta
books.subtitle: Italy Didn't Invent It and That's Just the Beginning
books.description: The Chinese were eating noodles 4,000 years before Marco Polo allegedly brought pasta to Italy. The origin story most people know is almost entirely myth. 100 tangled facts about the world's most consumed staple.

books.title: 100 Facts About Bacon
books.subtitle: The Most Obsessed Over Food in Human History
books.description: Humans have been curing pork for over 3,000 years. In the modern era it has achieved a cultural status no other food has matched. 100 sizzling facts about the strip of meat that the world cannot stop talking about.

books.title: 100 Facts About Garlic
books.subtitle: Medicine, Magic and the World's Most Powerful Ingredient
books.description: Egyptian pyramid workers were paid in garlic. Roman soldiers ate it before battle. Modern science has confirmed properties that ancient medicine claimed for thousands of years. 100 pungent facts about the ingredient that has never gone out of style.

books.title: 100 Facts About Rum
books.subtitle: Pirates, Revolutions and the Most Notorious Drink Ever Made
books.description: It was the currency of the slave trade, the fuel of the British Navy, and the drink that bankrolled the American Revolution. 100 intoxicating facts about the spirit that built and broke empires.

books.title: 100 Facts About Hamburgers
books.subtitle: The Sandwich Nobody Wanted to Claim
books.description: Nobody agrees on who invented it. Germany claims it. America claims it. A county fair in Texas claims it. The truth is stranger than all of them. 100 surprising facts about the world's most contested sandwich.

books.title: 100 Facts About Kimchi
books.subtitle: Older Than Most Civilizations Still Standing
books.description: It has been fermenting in Korean culture for over 3,000 years. It went to space. UNESCO protected it. North and South Korea both claim they invented it. 100 pungent facts about the world's most fiercely defended dish.

books.title: 100 Facts About Tequila
books.subtitle: The Sacred Cactus Juice of Mexico
books.description: It is not made from a cactus. The agave plant takes 12 years to mature. The worm in the bottle is a marketing invention. 100 eye-opening facts about Mexico's most misunderstood spirit.

books.title: 100 Facts About Pretzels
books.subtitle: Baked by Monks, Eaten by Everyone
books.description: A monk baked the first pretzel as a reward for children who memorized their prayers. The twisted shape represents arms folded in devotion. It became the snack of empires. 100 twisted facts about the world's oldest baked treat.

books.title: 100 Facts About Vodka
books.subtitle: The Drink That Fueled a Revolution
books.description: Russia and Poland have been arguing over who invented it for 600 years. It funded the Soviet Union. It has been used as currency, medicine, and rocket fuel. 100 clear facts about the world's most politically charged spirit.

books.title: 100 Facts About Avocados
books.subtitle: The Ancient Fruit That Almost Vanished
books.description: It survived because one farmer in California refused to give up on it. The animals that spread its seeds went extinct 13,000 years ago. A global marketing conspiracy turned it into a lifestyle. 100 rich facts about the world's most complicated fruit.

books.title: 100 Facts About Croissants
books.subtitle: Not Actually French and Never Was
books.description: It was invented in Vienna, Austria. The French adopted it, refined it, and claimed it. The flaky layers were an accident. Marie Antoinette may have introduced it to Paris. 100 buttery facts about the pastry that lied about its passport.

books.title: 100 Facts About Spam
books.subtitle: The Tin That Conquered the Pacific
books.description: It was invented during the Great Depression. It fed Allied soldiers across three continents. Hawaii consumes more of it per capita than anywhere on Earth. 100 surprising facts about the canned meat the world cannot stop eating.

books.title: 100 Facts About Gin
books.subtitle: The Medicine That Destroyed a City
books.description: It was invented by a Dutch doctor as a kidney medicine. The British adopted it and nearly drank themselves into collapse. The Gin Craze of 1720s London killed thousands. 100 botanically rich facts about history's most turbulent spirit.

books.title: 100 Facts About Popcorn
books.subtitle: Five Thousand Years Before the Movies
books.description: The Aztecs used it in religious ceremonies. The first webcam was invented to monitor a popcorn machine. It is the only grain that explodes. 100 explosive facts about the world's oldest snack.

books.title: 100 Facts About Tacos
books.subtitle: Street Food That Defeated an Empire
books.description: The Spanish tried to eliminate it. The Aztecs invented it. America turned it into a billion-dollar industry and then argued about authenticity. 100 crunchy facts about the most resilient street food in history.

books.title: 100 Facts About Maple Syrup
books.subtitle: Canada's Liquid Gold and Dark Secret
books.description: Canada controls over 70 percent of the world's supply. There is a global strategic reserve guarded like a state secret. A heist once stole 3,000 tonnes of it. 100 sticky facts about the sweetest cartel on Earth.

books.title: 100 Facts About Bourbon
books.subtitle: Born in Kentucky, Claimed by Everyone
books.description: By law it can only be called bourbon if made in America. Kentucky produces 95 percent of the world's supply. A Baptist minister may have invented it by accident. 100 smooth facts about America's most fiercely protected spirit.

books.title: 100 Facts About Ketchup
books.subtitle: It Started as a Chinese Fish Sauce
books.description: The original ketchup had no tomatoes. It was a fermented fish sauce from China. British sailors brought it to Europe. The tomato version took another century to arrive. 100 saucy facts about the condiment with a secret identity.

books.title: 100 Facts About Champagne
books.subtitle: The Accidental Explosion in a Bottle
books.description: The bubbles were originally considered a defect. A monk tried for years to get rid of them. Napoleon took 36 bottles on every military campaign. 100 sparkling facts about the drink that turned a mistake into a celebration.

books.title: 100 Facts About Curry
books.subtitle: The Dish That Does Not Exist
books.description: There is no such thing as a curry plant. The word was invented by the British. India has thousands of distinct dishes that have nothing to do with each other. 100 spiced facts about the world's most misunderstood cuisine.

books.title: 100 Facts About Absinthe
books.subtitle: The Green Fairy Was Never the Problem
books.description: It was banned across Europe for causing hallucinations. Modern science proved the hallucinations never existed. The ban lasted 100 years anyway. 100 luminous facts about the most unfairly demonized drink in history.

books.title: 100 Facts About Mustard
books.subtitle: Rome's Favorite Weapon at the Table
books.description: Roman soldiers carried it into battle as medicine and seasoning. It is the world's oldest condiment. Dijon has legally protected its recipe for centuries. 100 sharp facts about the condiment that conquered every table on Earth.

books.title: 100 Facts About Caviar
books.subtitle: The Fish Egg That Built an Empire
books.description: Russian tsars controlled the global supply for centuries. The Soviet Union used it as a diplomatic weapon. The sturgeon that produces it is older than the dinosaurs. 100 glistening facts about the most expensive food on Earth.

books.title: 100 Facts About Cinnamon
books.subtitle: Wars Were Fought Over This Bark
books.description: The Portuguese invaded Sri Lanka for it. The Dutch massacred entire populations to control it. Medieval Europeans thought it came from giant bird nests in paradise. 100 aromatic facts about the spice that sparked empires.

books.title: 100 Facts About Worcestershire Sauce
books.subtitle: Nobody Knows What's Actually In It
books.description: It was invented by accident in a basement in Worcester, England. The original batch was deemed undrinkable and left to ferment for two years. The full recipe remains a trade secret. 100 mysterious facts about the sauce nobody can spell or explain.

books.title: 100 Facts About Doughnuts
books.subtitle: The Fried Ring That Won Two Wars
books.description: The hole was invented to solve a cooking problem. The Salvation Army handed them out to soldiers in World War I trenches. America consumes 10 billion of them every year. 100 glazed facts about the fried ring that became a cultural institution.

books.title: 100 Facts About Vanilla
books.subtitle: The World's Second Most Expensive Spice
books.description: It can only be pollinated by hand. A 12-year-old slave discovered how to do it in 1841. Madagascar controls 80 percent of global supply. 100 complex facts about the spice hiding behind its own reputation for simplicity.

books.title: 100 Facts About Peanut Butter
books.subtitle: Invented for People With No Teeth
books.description: A Canadian doctor invented it in 1884 as a protein source for patients who could not chew. Marcellus Edson patented the paste. Kellogg refined it. America turned it into an obsession. 100 sticky facts about the spread that conquered the world one sandwich at a time.

books.title: 100 Facts About Hot Dogs
books.subtitle: America's Favorite Mystery Meat
books.description: Nobody agrees what is actually in it. Frankfurt and Vienna both claim they invented it. Americans eat 20 billion of them every year. 100 snapping facts about the sausage that became a national symbol.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Ninja
books.subtitle: The Shadow Warriors of Feudal Japan
books.description: Most of what you know about ninjas is wrong. They rarely wore black, almost never fought samurai, and their most powerful weapon was information. 100 facts about the spies and saboteurs history turned into legends.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Roman Gladiator
books.subtitle: The Slaves Who Became the World's First Superstars
books.description: Their faces sold merchandise, their blood was used as medicine, and fans wrote their names on walls across the empire. Most gladiators survived their bouts. 100 facts about the reluctant celebrities of the ancient world.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Knight
books.subtitle: The Armored Warriors Who Dominated Medieval Warfare
books.description: Full plate armor weighed less than a modern soldier's combat gear and was easier to move in than most people think. Knights spent more time managing estates than fighting. 100 facts about the warrior class behind the legend.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Mongol Warrior
books.subtitle: The Riders Who Conquered More Land Than Anyone in History
books.description: In 25 years the Mongols conquered more territory than Rome did in 400. Their horses could survive on grass alone and their archers could fire backwards at full gallop. 100 facts about the most devastating military force in human history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Aztec Warrior
books.subtitle: The Sacred Soldiers Who Fought to Keep the Sun Alive
books.description: Aztec warriors were trained to capture enemies alive, not kill them — dead men could not feed the gods. The jaguar and eagle warriors were the most elite soldiers in Mesoamerica. 100 facts about the army that believed the universe depended on their victory.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Zulu Warrior
books.subtitle: The Army That Stopped a British Empire Cold
books.description: At Isandlwana in 1879, 20,000 Zulu warriors annihilated a British regiment armed with rifles and artillery. They did it with spears. 100 facts about the military genius that humiliated the most powerful empire on Earth.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Mamluk
books.subtitle: The Slave Soldiers Who Became Sultans
books.description: They were purchased as children, trained as warriors, and ended up ruling the empires that bought them. The Mamluks stopped both the Crusaders and the Mongols. 100 facts about the slave soldiers who became the most powerful force in the medieval Islamic world.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Roman Legionnaire
books.subtitle: The Soldier Who Marched Half the World Into Submission
books.description: A Roman legionnaire marched 20 miles a day in full armor and then built a fortified camp before sleeping. They constructed roads, aqueducts and cities between campaigns. 100 facts about the soldier who was equal parts warrior and engineer.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Apache Warrior
books.subtitle: The Unconquered Fighter of the American West
books.description: The US Army chased Geronimo and 38 Apache warriors with 5,000 soldiers and never caught them in the field. Apache warriors could run 70 miles in a day through desert terrain. 100 facts about the fighters who made the US military rethink everything it knew about war.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Gurkha
books.subtitle: The Mountain Warriors No Enemy Wanted to Face
books.description: When asked to choose between dying and surrendering, Gurkha soldiers have historically chosen death. Their curved kukri blade is still one of the most feared close-combat weapons in the world. 100 facts about the mountain warriors every army in history has wanted on their side.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Crusader
books.subtitle: The Warriors Who Marched Thousands of Miles for God
books.description: The First Crusade marched 3,000 miles on foot to reach Jerusalem and somehow won. Most crusaders never made it home and many had no idea where they were going. 100 facts about the holy wars that reshaped the medieval world and whose consequences never ended.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Immortals of Persia
books.subtitle: The Elite Force That Was Never Allowed to Shrink
books.description: The Persian Immortals were so named because their number never dropped below 10,000 — every fallen soldier was immediately replaced. They were the personal guard of the king and the tip of the most powerful empire on Earth. 100 facts about the elite force that gave Persia its edge.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Celtic Warrior
books.subtitle: The Wild Fighters Who Scared the Roman Army
books.description: Celtic warriors charged into battle naked, screaming, and covered in blue paint — and Roman soldiers genuinely feared them. They fought with swords so long they had to be bent to fit in their scabbards. 100 facts about the barbarians who gave Rome its greatest nightmares.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Maori Warrior
books.subtitle: The People No Empire Ever Conquered
books.description: The British Empire conquered a quarter of the world but never subdued the Maori. The haka was not just a dance — it was a declaration of war, a challenge, and a weapon of psychological terror. 100 facts about the warriors who forced the most powerful empire in history to negotiate.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Ottoman Warrior
books.subtitle: The Soldiers Who Ruled Three Continents
books.description: The Ottoman Janissaries were taken from Christian families as boys, converted, and turned into the most disciplined soldiers in the medieval world. They eventually became powerful enough to make and unmake sultans. 100 facts about the military machine behind six centuries of empire.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Cataphract
books.subtitle: The Ancient World's Most Devastating Armored Cavalry
books.description: Both horse and rider were encased in overlapping metal scales from head to hoof — the ancient world's equivalent of a tank. Cataphracts were used from Persia to Rome to Byzantium for over a thousand years. 100 facts about the armored cavalry that dominated ancient battlefields.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Hussar
books.subtitle: Europe's Most Daring Cavalry Warriors
books.description: They wore leopard skins, fake wings that screamed in the wind, and rode straight at cannons without flinching. The Polish Winged Hussars destroyed a Swedish army three times their size at Kircholm. 100 facts about the most flamboyant and fearless cavalry in European history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Shaolin Monk
books.subtitle: The Monks Who Turned the Body Into a Weapon
books.description: Shaolin monks trained for decades to condition their bodies to withstand blows that would kill ordinary men — and then went to war for Chinese emperors. Their martial arts tradition is over 1,500 years old. 100 facts about the warriors who found enlightenment through combat.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Sikh Warrior
books.subtitle: The Khalsa Soldiers Who Never Surrendered
books.description: The Khalsa warrior code demands that a Sikh soldier never retreats, never surrenders, and never abandons a fellow fighter. The British considered them the finest soldiers they ever faced in India. 100 facts about the warrior faith that turned spiritual devotion into military legend.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Rajput Warrior
books.subtitle: The Warrior Kings Who Chose Death Before Defeat
books.description: When a Rajput fort was about to fall, the women performed Jauhar — mass self-immolation — while the men rode out in saffron robes to die fighting rather than surrender. 100 facts about the warrior clans whose code of honor made defeat unthinkable.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Maratha Warrior
books.subtitle: The Army That Humbled the Mughal Empire
books.description: From a small mountain kingdom in the Deccan, the Marathas built an empire that stretched across most of the Indian subcontinent and brought the Mughal Empire to its knees. 100 facts about the guerrilla commanders who changed the course of Indian history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Dahomey Amazon
books.subtitle: The Women Who Chose War Over Everything Else
books.description: The Agojie were the only standing all-female military unit in modern history — and they were considered the most feared soldiers in the Kingdom of Dahomey. French Foreign Legion veterans said they were the toughest opponents they ever faced. 100 facts about the women who made war their life.

books.title: 100 Facts About Thor
books.subtitle: The Norse God of Thunder and Lightning
books.description: Thor once dressed as a bride to retrieve his stolen hammer from a giant — and ate an entire ox at the wedding feast before anyone noticed. He was not the sharpest god on Asgard but he was the strongest. 100 facts about the hammer-wielding son of Odin history never stopped loving.

books.title: 100 Facts About Hercules
books.subtitle: The Demigod Famous for His Twelve Labors
books.description: Hercules was assigned his twelve labors as punishment for killing his own family in a fit of madness sent by Hera. He completed tasks that gods said were impossible, including holding up the sky. 100 facts about the demigod whose strength was matched only by his suffering.

books.title: 100 Facts About Quetzalcoatl
books.subtitle: The Feathered Serpent God of the Aztecs
books.description: Quetzalcoatl was so beloved that when the Spanish arrived, some Aztecs believed Cortes was the god returning — a myth the Spanish themselves encouraged to justify conquest. He was the god of wind, learning, and the morning star. 100 facts about the feathered serpent at the heart of Mesoamerican civilization.

books.title: 100 Facts About Poseidon
books.subtitle: The Greek God Who Controlled the Seas
books.description: Poseidon lost the contest for Athens to Athena and spent centuries making the city's life miserable in revenge. He created horses, caused earthquakes, and held grudges longer than any other Olympian. 100 facts about the sea god whose temper shaped the ancient world.

books.title: 100 Facts About Loki
books.subtitle: The Norse Trickster Who Triggered Ragnarok
books.description: Loki helped the gods solve their problems for centuries — and then personally engineered the death of Odin's favorite son and the destruction of the entire Norse universe. He was not evil at first. 100 facts about mythology's most complicated character.

books.title: 100 Facts About Achilles
books.subtitle: The Greek Hero with One Fatal Weakness
books.description: Achilles knew he was going to die at Troy before he ever left home — and went anyway because glory mattered more than survival. His rage over a stolen slave girl nearly lost the Greeks the entire war. 100 facts about the greatest warrior in Greek mythology and the choices that destroyed him.

books.title: 100 Facts About Ra
books.subtitle: The Egyptian Sun God Who Never Rested
books.description: Every night Ra sailed through the underworld in a boat, battling the serpent Apophis to ensure the sun would rise again. Egyptians believed that if Ra ever lost that battle, the world would end permanently. 100 facts about the sun god whose endless journey kept the universe alive.

books.title: 100 Facts About Athena
books.subtitle: The Greek Goddess Born Ready for War
books.description: Athena burst fully grown and fully armed from Zeus's skull after he swallowed her pregnant mother whole. She was the goddess of wisdom and war but never lost a battle or a debate. 100 facts about the most formidable mind on Mount Olympus.

books.title: 100 Facts About Amaterasu
books.subtitle: The Japanese Sun Goddess of the Imperial Line
books.description: When Amaterasu hid in a cave after her brother's rampage, the world went dark and crops failed — until the other gods threw a party so loud outside that her curiosity got the better of her. Every Japanese emperor claims direct descent from her. 100 facts about the sun goddess at the heart of Japanese civilization.

books.title: 100 Facts About Hades
books.subtitle: The Greek God Who Ruled the Underworld
books.description: Hades was not evil — he was simply the god nobody wanted to think about. He ruled the dead fairly, rarely left the underworld, and was one of the least troublesome Olympians. 100 facts about the most misrepresented god in Greek mythology.

books.title: 100 Facts About Apollo
books.subtitle: The Greek God of Light and Prophecy
books.description: Apollo's oracle at Delphi was consulted by kings and generals for over a thousand years — and the answers were always technically true but almost never what anyone expected. He was also responsible for the Trojan War's outcome. 100 facts about the most versatile and dangerous god on Olympus.

books.title: 100 Facts About Gilgamesh
books.subtitle: The World's Oldest Documented Hero
books.description: The Epic of Gilgamesh was written 1,500 years before Homer and contains a flood story almost identical to Noah's ark. Gilgamesh was two-thirds god and spent his life searching for immortality — and failed. 100 facts about the first hero in recorded human history.

books.title: 100 Facts About Ares
books.subtitle: The Greek God Even Olympians Feared
books.description: Ares was the god of war but he lost almost every battle he personally entered — including being wounded by a mortal during the Trojan War. The other Olympians despised him, including his own parents. 100 facts about the most hated god on Mount Olympus.

books.title: 100 Facts About Freya
books.subtitle: The Norse Goddess of Love and War
books.description: Freya had first pick of the dead from every battlefield — she took half before Odin got any. She was also the goddess of love, fertility, and magic, and she cried tears of gold when separated from those she loved. 100 facts about the most powerful goddess in Norse mythology.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Minotaur
books.subtitle: The Half-Bull Monster of the Cretan Labyrinth
books.description: The Minotaur existed because Poseidon cursed King Minos for refusing to sacrifice a bull — a chain of divine grudges that ended with Athens sending fourteen teenagers to be eaten every nine years. 100 facts about the monster at the center of one of mythology's darkest stories.

books.title: 100 Facts About Set
books.subtitle: The Egyptian God of Chaos and Storms
books.description: Set murdered his own brother Osiris, dismembered the body and scattered the pieces across Egypt — and still managed to remain a respected god for centuries before being recast as pure evil. 100 facts about the Egyptian god whose reputation got progressively worse for three thousand years.

books.title: 100 Facts About Odysseus
books.subtitle: The Greek Hero of the Ten-Year Odyssey
books.description: Odysseus took ten years to sail home from Troy — a journey that should have taken weeks. He outsmarted a Cyclops, escaped a sorceress, visited the underworld, and still made it back. 100 facts about the cleverest and most human of all the Greek heroes.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Morrigan
books.subtitle: The Celtic Goddess of War and Fate
books.description: The Morrigan did not fight battles — she decided who would survive them. She appeared as a crow circling dying warriors and her favor was the most coveted and most feared thing a Celtic hero could receive. 100 facts about the shapeshifting goddess who controlled the outcome of every Irish war.

books.title: 100 Facts About Aphrodite
books.subtitle: The Goddess of Love Behind the Trojan War
books.description: Aphrodite started the Trojan War by bribing a mortal prince with the world's most beautiful woman — who happened to already be married to a king. Ten years, thousands of deaths, and a burning city later, she faced no consequences. 100 facts about the most dangerous goddess in Greek mythology.

books.title: 100 Facts About Perseus
books.subtitle: The Greek Hero Who Defeated Medusa
books.description: Perseus was conceived when Zeus visited his mother as a shower of gold, raised in a wooden chest at sea, and sent on a suicide mission by a king who expected him to die. He came back with a severed head that turned his enemies to stone. 100 facts about the original Greek hero who did everything right.

books.title: 100 Facts About Hera
books.subtitle: The Queen of the Greek Gods
books.description: Hera was the goddess of marriage and spent most of her existence punishing women her husband seduced and children he fathered. She tormented Hercules his entire life for the crime of being born. 100 facts about the most powerful and most wronged goddess on Mount Olympus.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Siberian Husky
books.subtitle: The Arctic Sled Dog Built to Survive the Impossible
books.description: A team of Siberian Huskies ran 658 miles through an Alaskan blizzard in 1925 to deliver diphtheria antitoxin to a dying city — in five and a half days. Their metabolism can shift into a fat-burning mode that allows them to run indefinitely without hitting a wall. 100 facts about the sled dog built for conditions that would kill anything else.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Dachshund
books.subtitle: The Badger Hunter with the Most Recognizable Body in the World
books.description: The Dachshund's elongated body and short legs were deliberately bred so it could dig into badger burrows and fight the animal underground. That same body shape now makes them one of the world's most popular companion dogs. 100 facts about the dog whose entire anatomy was designed for a fight most people have forgotten about.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Poodle
books.subtitle: The Dog Behind the Curls That Was Bred for the Hunt
books.description: The Poodle's famous show cut was originally a practical hunting modification — the pompoms were left to protect joints and vital organs from cold water while excess fur was shaved to reduce drag. They are the second most intelligent dog breed ever tested. 100 facts about the hunting dog the world decided to dress up instead.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Beagle
books.subtitle: The Nose on Four Legs That Changed Scientific History
books.description: Charles Darwin sailed around the world on a ship called the Beagle, and the breed itself has one of the most powerful noses in the dog world — with 220 million scent receptors compared to a human's 5 million. The US Department of Agriculture uses Beagles to detect illegal food items at airports. 100 facts about the small dog with the most powerful nose on four legs.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Rottweiler
books.subtitle: The Roman Cattle Dog Built for Protection
books.description: Roman legions used Rottweiler ancestors to herd cattle across the Alps to feed their armies — and those same dogs guarded the meat at night. After the Roman Empire fell, they kept working in the German town of Rottweil for another thousand years. 100 facts about one of the oldest working dog breeds on Earth.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Border Collie
books.subtitle: The Most Intelligent Dog Breed Ever Documented
books.description: A Border Collie named Chaser learned the names of 1,022 individual objects — more than any other non-human animal ever tested. The breed can anticipate sheep movements before they happen and has been clocked herding at over 30 miles per hour. 100 facts about the dog that makes every other breed look like it is not trying.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Doberman
books.subtitle: The Breed Created by a Tax Collector Who Needed Protection
books.description: Louis Dobermann was a tax collector in 19th century Germany who needed a dog intimidating enough to protect him on his rounds — so he bred one from scratch. The resulting dog became one of the most effective military and police breeds ever developed. 100 facts about the breed one man invented for his own personal security.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Great Dane
books.subtitle: The Gentle Giant That Once Stood Taller Than Most Humans
books.description: The tallest dog ever recorded was a Great Dane named Zeus who stood 44 inches at the shoulder — taller than most children and many adults when standing on his hind legs. Despite their size, they are one of the most gentle and people-dependent breeds in existence. 100 facts about the dog that is somehow both the largest and the most affectionate.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Shiba Inu
books.subtitle: Japan's Oldest and Most Ancient Dog Breed
books.description: The Shiba Inu is one of the oldest dog breeds on Earth, with DNA evidence tracing its lineage back over 9,000 years. It nearly went extinct during World War II and was saved by a coordinated national breeding program. 100 facts about the ancient Japanese dog that became a global internet phenomenon.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Pitbull
books.subtitle: The Most Misunderstood Dog Breed in the World
books.description: Pitbulls were once called nanny dogs in America and trusted to watch over children — their temperament tests consistently score higher than Golden Retrievers. Breed-specific legislation has banned them in dozens of countries based on statistics that don't hold up to scientific scrutiny. 100 facts about the dog whose reputation has almost nothing to do with its actual nature.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Boxer
books.subtitle: The Dog That Fought in Two World Wars
books.description: Boxers served as messenger dogs, pack carriers, and attack dogs in both World Wars — and were among the first breeds trained as guide dogs for the blind in the aftermath. They get their name not from the sport but from their habit of batting objects with their front paws. 100 facts about one of the most versatile working dogs of the 20th century.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Chihuahua
books.subtitle: The World's Smallest Dog with the Biggest Personality
books.description: The Chihuahua is the world's smallest dog breed but has a larger brain-to-body ratio than almost any other breed — which may explain why they are so convinced they are in charge. Archaeological evidence suggests their ancestors were sacred dogs in the Toltec civilization over a thousand years ago. 100 facts about the tiny dog with no idea how small it is.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Australian Shepherd
books.subtitle: The American-Born Dog That Was Never Australian
books.description: The Australian Shepherd was developed entirely in the American West and has almost no connection to Australia — the name came from the Basque shepherds who brought their dogs from Australia during the Gold Rush. It became the cowboy's dog of choice across the American frontier. 100 facts about the breed with the most misleading name in dog history.

books.title: 100 Facts About The Bulldog
books.subtitle: The Dog That Became the Symbol of British Determination
books.description: The original Bulldog was bred to bite a bull's nose and hang on until the animal collapsed — a sport called bull-baiting that was banned in 1835.
